humanLabor.comment: Societal time in paid/necessary labor ≈10% of the unit time budget (stylized; residual freeTime absorbs the rest with basicNeeds/leisure).

basicNeeds.comment: Floor for health/education/etc.; matches minOutput and a ~10% time/energy commitment.

electric_transport.comment: Light-duty EV stock share order-of-magnitude (~20% of LDV energy service), not 0/100 corner from free optimization.

heavy_electric_transport.comment: Heavy-duty road electrification still near-zero of freight energy service today.

humanLabor.comment: Small labor share of wellhead energy cost; oil & gas EROI literature places most investment in fuels, electricity and materials rather than human work (Sustainability 2022 EROI harmonization; arXiv:2606.02015 on extraction self-use).

fuels.comment: Direct diesel/fuel for drilling, pumping and gathering; typical extraction self-consumption is a few % of gross output (Nature Energy 2024 useful-stage EROI; IEA energy industry own-use).

electricity.comment: Grid/field electricity for pumps and compressors treated as external input to oil & gas (arXiv:2606.02015 EXT formulation).

mining.comment: Embodied materials and equipment intensity at the wellhead; kept low so total TRE ≈0.11 → EROI~9, within harmonized petroleum ranges before refining (Sustainability 2022).

humanLabor.comment: Underground/surface mining remains relatively labor-intensive vs oil & gas; modest labor TRE share (Sustainability 2022 EROI review).

fuels.comment: Diesel for haul trucks, dozers and prep plants; mining self-use is a few percent of coal energy content (IEA energy industry own-use; Nature Energy 2024).

electricity.comment: Mine electricity for ventilation, conveyors and prep; external input analogous to oil & gas EXT accounting (arXiv:2606.02015).

mining.comment: Steel, explosives and capital goods embodied energy for mine infrastructure; small vs fuel self-use (harmonized fossil EROI literature).

humanLabor.comment: Refinery staffing is small relative to feedstock energy throughput; residual labor TRE (Argonne/Wang refining studies).

petroleum.comment: U.S. refining overall energy efficiency ~90–91% → ~1.10–1.11 MJ crude per MJ products (Wang et al. EST 2014; ANL refining efficiency ~90.8%).

electricity.comment: Purchased/on-site electricity and utilities are a minor but non-zero share of refinery process energy (PRELIM model; Wang et al. EST 2014 product-specific intensities).

humanLabor.comment: Plant O&M labor is small vs fuel heat input for thermal generation.

coal.comment: Existing coal fleet net heat rate ~9–11k Btu/kWh ≈ 31–38% efficiency → coal TRE ≈2.6–3.2; 3.0 ≈ ~33% industry-average heat rate (Power Magazine; ADEQ/EPA ~10,100–10,300 Btu/kWh).

mining.comment: Ash handling, pollution-control materials and plant capital embodied energy, small vs fuel (LCA of coal power).

humanLabor.comment: Install/O&M labor slightly higher share than thermal fuel plants because fuel TRE is replaced by capital (IEA-PVPS NEA guidelines).

mining.comment: Embodied materials/BOS; PV meta-analyses imply EROI often ~8–25 → investment ~0.04–0.12 of lifetime output (Ellingson & Apul 2015; IEA-PVPS Task 12).

sun.comment: Ambient primary harvest normalized to 1 unit of renewable electricity carrier in this TRE graph (IEA-PVPS net-energy guidelines).

humanLabor.comment: Industry remains labor-using; ~10% of industrial-output TRE as labor services in this stylized basket.

electricity.comment: Electricity dominates modern manufacturing and minerals processing energy; set at 1 unit primary electricity per unit industrial output (IEA industry energy balances).

heavy_transport.comment: Freight of ores, intermediates and finished goods; freight is a meaningful but secondary share of industrial energy (IEA transport + industry balances).

humanLabor.comment: Farm and food-chain labor; on-farm energy is minority of agri-food energy but labor remains essential (IIASA food-chain energy; FAO ~30% of world energy in food system).

heavy_transport.comment: Transport ~14% of US food-system energy; elevated here because model folds distribution into agriculture node (GRAIN/FAO food-system energy; OECD agro-food chain).

mining.comment: Fertilizers, machinery and packaging embodied energy; fertilizer alone ~40% of on-farm energy and chemicals/machinery dominate pre-harvest (GRAIN summarizing US food LCA).

humanLabor.comment: Driver/crew labor small vs fuel for light-duty thermal transport.

fuels.comment: ICE tank-to-wheel often wastes 64–75% of fuel energy → TRE ~3–4; 3.2 is mid-range (DOE fueleconomy.gov loss shares; NREL EVER study context).

mining.comment: Vehicle manufacturing embodied energy amortized per unit transport service (vehicle LCA).

humanLabor.comment: Similar crew/operations labor share as thermal LDV service.

electricity.comment: US light-duty EVER ≈4.4 vs gasoline → electricity TRE ≈ thermal_fuels/4.4; with fuels≈3.2 → ≈0.73, set 0.75 with charger margin (NREL/DOE EVER 4.4 report).

mining.comment: Battery and powertrain manufacturing raise embodied intensity vs ICE (EV LCA literature; Yale Climate Connections WTW caveats).

humanLabor.comment: Crew labor small vs diesel for heavy freight.

fuels.comment: Heavy diesel duty cycles similar TTW inefficiency class to LDV ICE (~3–4 TRE); aligned with thermal_transport (DOE engine efficiency ranges).

mining.comment: Trucks/rail rolling stock capital intensity slightly above LDV per service unit.

humanLabor.comment: Operations labor comparable to heavy thermal freight.

electricity.comment: Rail/truck electrification is more efficient than diesel but model keeps ≥1 electricity TRE plus high capital; conservative vs LDV EVER (IEA truck/rail electrification).

mining.comment: Batteries, catenary and heavy EV powertrains: capital embodied energy dominates vs LDV electric (heavy-duty EV LCA).

fuels.comment: Condensing gas boilers ~90–98% → TRE≈1.02–1.11; 1.15 reflects seasonal and distribution losses on a mostly modern stock (UK BEIS/ASHP vs boiler comparisons; heatpumpswatch efficiency notes).

mining.comment: Boiler/furnace and distribution hardware embodied energy.

electricity.comment: Direct electric heating COP≈1. Heat pumps SPF~2.8–3.5 would need ~0.3–0.4 electricity if ambient heat were credited; without ambient node we keep resistive-equivalent 1 (BEIS SPF ~3.2 ASHP; UCL heat-pump LCA).

mining.comment: Heaters/heat-pump hardware embodied energy; similar order to thermal plant capital in this stylized model.

heating.comment: Space/water heat is often the largest residential energy end-use in temperate climates; ~1/4 of labor-support basket (IEA buildings end-use shares).

electricity.comment: Appliances, lighting and services for workers; secondary to heat/food in household energy (IEA buildings).

mining.comment: Goods, tools and housing materials supporting labor capacity (industrial output share of living standards).

transport.comment: Commuting and work-related mobility; transport is a major household energy use after heating (IEA transport + buildings).

food.comment: Food system uses ~26–30% of primary energy in rich economies; largest single share of the labor-support basket (FAO/GRAIN; IIASA food-chain energy).

heating.comment: Hospitals, schools and housing heat loads; heating remains a large buildings share (IEA buildings).

electricity.comment: Electrified services (health IT, lighting, ventilation) raise electricity vs pure household labor basket.

mining.comment: Medical equipment, school materials and infrastructure embodied intensity (small share).

humanLabor.comment: Care, teaching and public-service labor required to deliver basic needs.

transport.comment: Patient/student/staff mobility and logistics for public services.

food.comment: Nutrition floor of basic needs; aligned with food-system energy weight in living standards (FAO ~30% energy in food system).

heating.comment: Leisure buildings/venues heat; smaller share than labor/basic-needs baskets.

mining.comment: Durable leisure goods and military capital embodied energy (stylized ‘leisure/war’ sink).

humanLabor.comment: Leisure services and force structure are labor-heavy relative to energy carriers in this sink.

food.comment: Food associated with leisure/hospitality beyond the basic-needs floor.
